purpose: This medicine is used to treat serious heart failure when your heart is not pumping blood strongly enough. It helps your heart work better and makes it easier for blood to flow through your body. It is given in a hospital setting through an IV line directly into your vein.
how_it_works: Milrinone works by blocking a specific enzyme in your heart called phosphodiesterase-3, which allows certain natural chemicals in your heart to build up. These chemicals cause your heart muscle to squeeze more strongly and pump more blood with each beat. At the same time, it helps relax and widen your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to push blood through.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is an irregular or fast heartbeat, which your medical team will watch closely. You may also experience low blood pressure, headache, or chest pain. Some people notice their heart beating unusually hard or feel lightheaded during treatment.
warnings: This medication can cause serious irregular heart rhythms, so you will be on a heart monitor the entire time you receive it. It should be used very carefully in people with kidney problems, as the dose may need to be adjusted. Tell your doctor right away if you feel your heart racing, have trouble breathing, or feel very dizzy or faint. This medicine is only given in a hospital by trained medical staff.
typical_dosing: The dose is carefully calculated based on your body weight and how sick your heart is. It is usually started as a slow loading dose given over about 10 minutes, followed by a continuous drip through your IV that can last up to a few days. Your doctors and nurses will adjust the drip rate based on how your heart is responding.
